title: Piecewise functions, absolute value, floor, and graph transformations
section: Graphs in the xy-Plane ▷ Piecewise graphs
terms: piecewise function; absolute value; greatest integer function; floor; step function; transla- tion; scaling.

exposition.text:
A piecewise function uses different formulas on specified parts of its domain; endpoint inequal-
ities determine which value is assigned at a boundary. Absolute value is |x| = x for x ≥ 0 and
−x for x < 0. The floor ⌊x⌋ is the greatest integer no larger than x, so ⌊−1.2⌋ = −2. A step
function is constant on intervals but can jump between them.
The graph of y = af(b(x − h)) + k shifts by (h, k), scales vertically by |a| and horizontally
by 1/|b|, and reflects when a multiplier is negative. For absolute-value equations, split at zeros
of the enclosed expressions; retain each algebraic solution only if it lies in the interval used to
derive it. Floor equations are solved by inequalities n ≤ x < n + 1.

question.text:
What is the total length of the set of real numbers satisfying ⌊x⌋ + ⌊2x⌋ = 7?
(A) 0 (B) 1/4 (C) 1/2 (D) 1 (E) 3/2

solution.text:
Write x = n + t with integer n and 0 ≤ t < 1. The equation is 3n + ⌊2t⌋ = 7. Since ⌊2t⌋ is 0
or 1, only n = 2 and 1/2 ≤ t < 1 work. The solution interval is [5/2, 3), of length 1/2.

question.text:
What is the sum of all real solutions of |x − 2| + 2|x + 1| = 7?
(A) −4 (B) −2 (C) 0 (D) 2 (E) 4

solution.text:
For x < −1, the equation is −3x = 7, giving x = −7/3. For −1 ≤ x ≤ 2, it is x + 4 = 7,
whose candidate 3 is outside the interval. For x > 2, it is 3x = 7, giving 7/3. Their sum is
0.

The terms are 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, whose sum is 37. Grouping four consecutive indices
also exposes the pattern.

question.text:
What is the minimum of |x − 1| + |x − 4| + |x − 9| over real x?
(A) 6 (B) 7 (C) 8 (D) 5 (E) 9

solution.text:
The median x = 4 minimizes the sum. On [1, 4] the slope is −1, and on [4, 9] it is 1; outside
this interval the sum is larger. Its value at 4 is 8.

question.text:
A function f has a unique global maximum f (−2) = 5. Define g(x) = 7 − 3f (4 − 2x). At which
point does g attain its global minimum?
(A) (−2, −8) (B) (3, −8) (C) (3, 22) (D) (0, −8) (E) (−3, −8)

solution.text:
Multiplication by −3 converts the maximum into a minimum. Solve 4 − 2x = −2 to obtain
x = 3; the output is 7 − 3(5) = −8. Because 4 − 2x maps R bijectively onto R, the minimum
remains unique.
